# Show HN post

**Title:** Show HN: ciburn - what your GitHub Actions CI costs, from your own run history

Across 1699 public repositories (56,682 sampled jobs), 7.5 % of billed GitHub Actions minutes were never executed. GitHub rounds every job up to a whole minute, and 47.6 % of jobs finish in under one. For the median repository that rounding is 21.7 % of its bill; at the 90th percentile, 63.1 %.

ciburn is a Python CLI that reads .github/workflows, joins each finding to the repository's actual runs, jobs and steps, and prices them under GitHub's 2026 rates. Every number is an observed measurement or an estimate that states its method. No LLM, no service, no telemetry.

Also in the corpus: 71.8 % of repositories cache dependencies (ICSE 2024: 32.9 % of paid-tier repos); 3.1 % set timeout-minutes on every job; 132 of 776 repositories with schedules have a cron that failed three or more times in a row.

Dataset, method and limitations are in the repo. Figures are list-price equivalents; public repos pay nothing.

https://github.com/addiiiooo/ciburn
